semin-durr:1-1.t: His saying: {والطور}: it and what follows are oaths whose answer is {إِنَّ عَذَابَ رَبِّكَ لَوَاقِعٌ} [الطور: 7]. The «واو»s after the first are conjunctions, not particles of oath, for the reason I gave at the beginning of this topic on the authority of al-Khalīl. He made «الكتاب» indefinite for magnification and exaltation.

semin-durr:3-3.t: His saying: {فِي رَقٍّ}: It is permissible that it be attached to «مَسْطُور», that is, "written on a parchment". Abū al-Baqāʾ allowed that it be another naʿt (adjective) of «كتابٍ»; there is room for objection in this, because it resembles preparing a governor for work and then cutting it off from it. «الرَقُّ» with fatḥa is the thin skin on which one writes. Al-Rāghib said: "«الرَّقُّ» is what one writes on, something like paper." End. So it is more general than being skin or something else. It is also said «رِقٌّ» with kasra; but as for ownership of slaves, it is said only «رِقٌّ» with kasra. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "«الرَّقُّ» is the sheet. It was also said: the skin on which [deeds] are written." End. Some have called wrong the one who says «كتبْتُ في الرِّق» with kasra, but it is not wrong, since it is established in the language with kasra. Abū al-Sammāl read «في رِقّ» with kasra.

semin-durr:6-6.t: His saying: {المسجور}: It was said to be one of the words with opposite meanings (aḍdād). It is said «بحر مَسْجور», that is, full, and «بحرٌ مَسْجور», that is, empty. The poet Dhū al-Rumma narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās that he said: a slave-girl went out to draw water and said: "The trough is «مَسْجور»", meaning empty. This is supported by the fact that the seas' water will go away on the Day of Resurrection. It was also said: «المسجور» is "held in", and from it comes «ساجور الكلب» (the dog's collar), because it holds and restrains it.

semin-durr:7-7.t: Zayd ibn ʿAlī read «إِنَّ عَذَابَ رَبِّكَ وَاقِعٌ» without the «لام».

semin-durr:8-8.t: His saying: {مَّا لَهُ مِن دَافِعٍ}: It is permissible that the clause be a second khabar (predicate), and that it be an adjective of «واقعٌ», that is, "occurring, not to be repelled"; Abū al-Baqāʾ said this. «مِنْ دافِع» may be the fāʿil (agent) or a mubtadaʾ (subject), with «مِنْ» redundant (zāʾida) on both views.

semin-durr:9-9.t:
His saying: {يَوْمَ تَمُورُ}: It is permissible that the governor of it be «واقعٌ», that is, "it will occur on that day"; on this, the negated clause is parenthetical between the governor and what it governs. It is also permissible that its governor be «دافعٌ»; al-Ḥawfī and Abū al-Baqāʾ said this, and Makkī forbade it. The Shaykh said: "He did not mention the evidence for the prohibition." I say: he did mention the evidence for the prohibition in «al-Kashf», though it may be an error in him, for it is a slip, and I will quote his wording to you. He, may Allah have mercy on him, said: "The governor of it is «واقعٌ», that is, 'The punishment of your Lord will occur on the day the sky sways with a swaying.' «دافعٌ» does not govern it, because a negated element does not govern what comes before the negator. You do not say «طعامَك ما زيدٌ آكلاً», whether you make «آكلاً» nominative, accusative, or bring «الباء» upon it. If you make «الطعام» nominative by the mubtadaʾ and apply «آكلاً» to a «هاء», it is allowed, and what comes after «الطعام» is the khabar." End. This is a sound statement in itself, except that nothing of that is in the verse, because the governor, which is «دافعٌ», and the governed, which is «يومَ», are both after the negator and within its scope. And his saying "and you applied «آكلاً» to a «هاء»" means to a pronoun returning to the food, so you say «طعامَك ما زيدٌ آكلَه».
It may be said: the reason for the prohibition is fear of a false impression, that it might be understood that someone could repel the punishment on a day other than that day, whereas the premise is that Allah's punishment is not repelled at any time. This is a fitting point, and many similar cases have been mentioned; for that reason some forbade that {يَوْمَ تَجِدُ كُلُّ نَفْسٍ} be accusative by His saying {والله على كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ} [آل عمران: 29-30], lest something unfitting be understood from it, which is much more remote in impression than this. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It was also said: it may be an adverbial for what «فوَيْلٌ» indicates." End; this is far-fetched.
«المَوْرُ» is agitation and movement; one says «مار الشيءُ», that is, it went and came. Al-Akhfash and Abū ʿUbayda said: it tilted. And he quoted al-Aʿshā:
4115 - كأن مِشْيتَها مِنْ بيتِ جارتِها ... مَوْرُ السَّحابةِ لا رَيْثٌ ولا عَجَلُ
(As if her walk from her neighbour's house were the drifting of a cloud, neither slow nor hasty.)
Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It was also said: it is movement in waviness, a thing moving to and fro sideways like the dāghiṣa." I say: «الداغِصَةُ» is the skin above the knee joint. Al-Rāghib said: "«المَوْرُ» is swift flowing. One says «مار الدمُ على وجهِه». And «المُوْرُ» with ḍamma is the dust that the wind moves back and forth." He emphasized with the two maṣdars (verbal nouns) to remove figurative reading, that is: these two great bodies, despite their density, will really do that.

semin-durr:11-11.t: His saying: {يَوْمَئِذٍ}: accusative by «وَيْل». The khabar (predicate) is «للمكذِّبين». As for the «فاء» in «فوَيْلٌ», Makkī said: "It is the answer to the preceding clause. This is good because the sentence contains the sense of a condition, for the meaning is: if what was mentioned occurs, then woe."

semin-durr:13-13.t:
His saying: {يَوْمَ يُدَعُّونَ}: It is permissible that it be an adverbial for an implied «يُقال» together with His saying «هذه النارُ», that is, "it will be said to them: this is the Fire, on the day they are thrust". It is also permissible that it be a badal (substitute) from His saying «يومَ تمور» or from «يومئذٍ» before it. The majority read it with fatḥa on the «دال» and shadda on the «عين», from «دَعَّه يَدُعُّه», that is, he pushed him in the chest violently and harshly. Al-Rāghib said: "Its origin is that one says to a stumbler «دَعْ دَعْ», as one says to him «لَعًا»"; this is far from the meaning of this word.
ʿAlī, al-Sulamī, Abū Rajāʾ and Zayd ibn ʿAlī read it with sukūn on the «دال» and light «عين» with fatḥa, from «الدعاء» (calling), that is, "they will be called to it, and it will be said to them: Come and enter it." «هذه النارُ» is a clause in the accusative position by an implied saying, that is, "the keepers will say to them: this is the Fire."

semin-durr:15-15.t: His saying: {أَفَسِحْرٌ}: a fronted khabar (predicate). «هذا» is a delayed mubtadaʾ (subject). The «فاء» has entered. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "He means: you used to say of the revelation: this is sorcery; so is this sorcery? He means: is this reality also sorcery? and the «فاء» entered for this meaning."

semin-durr:16-16.t: His saying: {سَوَآءٌ}: There are two views. The first: that it is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), that is, "your patience and leaving it are equal"; Abū al-Baqāʾ said this. The second: that it is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, that is, "patience and impatience are equal"; the Shaykh said this. The first is better, because making an indefinite noun the khabar is preferable to making it the mubtadaʾ and making a definite noun the khabar. Al-Zamakhsharī took the second course, saying: "«سواء» has its khabar omitted, that is, 'the two matters are equal for you: patience and its absence.'"

semin-durr:17-17.t: His saying: {إِنَّ المتقين فِي جَنَّاتٍ}: It is permissible that it be resumptive, the Exalted reporting that as glad tidings, and permissible that it be part of what is said to the disbelievers, to increase their distress and regret.

semin-durr:18-18.t:
His saying: {فَاكِهِينَ}: this is the reading of the majority; accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), and the khabar (predicate) is the adverbial. The owner of the ḥāl is the latent pronoun in the adverbial. Khālid read «فاكهون» nominative, so it is permissible that the adverbial be redundant, attached to the khabar, and permissible that it be another khabar according to those who allow multiple khabars. It was also read «فَكِهين» shortened. It will come that Ḥafṣ from ʿĀṣim read with it in al-Muṭaffifīn in the mutawātir reading.
His saying: {بِمَآ آتَاهُمْ}: It is permissible that the «باء» be in its original sense, and «ما» then refer to the fruits that are in Paradise, that is, "delighting in the fruit of Paradise". It is permissible that it have the sense of «في», that is, "in what He gave them of fruits and other things". It is also permissible that «ما» be a maṣdar particle.
His saying: {وَوَقَاهُمْ}: Several views are possible. The most apparent: that it is conjoined to the ṣila (relative clause), that is, "delighting in their Lord's giving them and in His protecting them from the punishment of Hell". The second: that the clause is a ḥāl, so «قد» is implied according to those who require it to accompany a past verb that occurs as a ḥāl. The third: that it is conjoined to «في جنات»; al-Zamakhsharī said this, meaning that it is also predicated of the God-fearing. The majority read the «قاف» light, from «الوِقاية»; Abū Ḥaywa read it with shadda.

semin-durr:19-19.t:
His saying: {كُلُواْ}: on the basis of an implied saying, as in His saying «هذه النار»; and how different the two sayings are!
His saying: {هَنِيئَاً}: what is said about it and about «مريئاً» was given in full in al-Nisāʾ. Al-Zamakhsharī said here: "It is said to them: eat and drink with wholesome eating and drinking, or wholesome food and drink, that is, one in which there is no vexation. It may be like what is in his saying:
4116 - هَنِيئاً مَرِيئاً غيرَ داءٍ مُخامِرٍ ... لِعَزَّةَ من أعراضِنا ما اسْتَحلَّتِ
(Wholesome and sweet, with no lingering ailment, to ʿAzza be what she deems lawful of our honour!)
I mean an attribute used in the manner of a maṣdar (verbal noun) standing in the place of the verb, with «ما استحلَّت» made nominative by it as it is by the verb, as if it were said: «هَنَأ عَزَّةَ المُسْتَحَلُّ من أعراضنا». Likewise the meaning of «هنيئاً» here is: eating and drinking have been wholesome for you, or what you used to do has been wholesome for you, that is, the reward of what you used to do; and the «باء» is redundant as in {وكفى بالله} [النساء: 45], and the «باء» is attached to «كلوا واشربوا» if you make the agent eating and drinking." I say: this is among the finest of his statements.
The Shaykh said: "As for his allowing the redundancy of the «باء», it is not regular in the agent except in the agent of «كفى», and even that is disputed, so allowing it here is not acceptable. And as for his saying that it is attached to «كلوا واشربوا», it is not valid except on the principle of iʿmāl (assigning to one of two competing governors), so it is attached to one of them." End. This is close.

semin-durr:20-20.t: His saying: {مُتَّكِئِينَ}: There are several views. The first: that it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of «كُلوا». The second: that it is a ḥāl from the object of «آتاهم». The third: that it is a ḥāl from the object of «وَقَاهم». The fourth: that it is a ḥāl from the latent pronoun in the adverbial. The fifth: that it is a ḥāl from the pronoun in «فاكهين». The best is that it be a ḥāl from the pronoun of the adverbial, because it is a mainstay of the sentence. «على سُرُر» is attached to «متكئين». The majority read it with ḍamma on the first «راء»; Abū al-Sammāl read it with fatḥa. It was mentioned earlier that it is a dialect of Kalb in doubled words, who avoid two successive ḍammas in a doubled word. ʿIkrima read «بحورِ عينٍ» with annexation of the qualified noun to its attribute, according to the well-known interpretation.

semin-durr:21-21.t:
His saying: {والذين آمَنُواْ}: There are three views. The first: that it is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the khabar (predicate) is the clause {أَلْحَقْنَا بِهِمْ ذُرِّيَّتَهُمْ}; and «الذُّرِّيَّةُ» here applies to fathers and to sons, that is, when the believer's deed is greater, the one lower than him in deed is joined to him, whether a son or a father. This is reported from Ibn ʿAbbās and others. The second: that it is accusative by an implied verb. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "on the implication «وأكرَمْنا الذين آمنوا»." I say: it is possible that he means it is a case of ishtighāl, and that His saying {أَلْحَقْنَا بِهِمْ ذُرِّيَّتَهُمْ} explains that verb in meaning; and possible that he means it is implied because the context indicates it, in which case the matter is not one of ishtighāl at all.
The third: that it is genitive, conjoined to «حورٍ عينٍ». Al-Zamakhsharī said: "«والذين آمنوا» is conjoined to «حورٍ عينٍ», that is, we paired them with the houris and with those who believed, that is, with the companions and associates among them, as in His saying {إِخْوَاناً على سُرُرٍ مُّتَقَابِلِينَ} [الحجر: 47]; so they will enjoy at one time playing with the houris and at another the company of brothers." Then al-Zamakhsharī said: "Then the Exalted said {بِإِيمَانٍ أَلْحَقْنَا بِهِمْ ذُرِّيَّتَهُمْ}, that is, because of a great faith, lofty in rank, which is the faith of the fathers, we joined their offspring to their rank, even though they do not merit it, as a favour upon them."
The Shaykh said: "No one imagines that «والذين آمنوا» is conjoined to «بحورٍ عينٍ» except this man, and it is the imagining of a non-Arab, contrary to the understanding of the pure Arab Ibn ʿAbbās and others." I say: as for the meaning Abū al-Qāsim mentioned, there is no doubt of its beauty and freshness, and nothing in the speech of a pure Arab refutes it; rather, had it been presented to Ibn ʿAbbās and others, it would have pleased them. And what obstacle, in meaning or in grammar, prevents it?
His saying: {واتبعتهم}: It is permissible that it be conjoined to the ṣila (relative clause), with «والذين» a mubtadaʾ, and that «بإيمان» be attached to the following, in the sense that Allah the Exalted joins the young children, even if they have not reached faith, to the rulings of the believing fathers. This meaning is reported from Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Ḍaḥḥāk. It is also permissible that it be parenthetical between the mubtadaʾ and the khabar; al-Zamakhsharī said this. It is permissible that «بإيمان» be attached to «ألحَقْنا», as mentioned. If it is said: His saying «اتَّبَعتْهم ذُرِّيَّتَهم» gives the same benefit as His saying {أَلْحَقْنَا بِهِمْ ذُرِّيَّتَهُمْ}, the answer is that His saying «ألحَقْنا بهم» is in the ranks, whereas the following is in the ruling of faith, even if they have not reached it, as mentioned. Abū ʿAmr read «وأَتْبَعْناهم» with the verb attributed to the speaker who magnifies himself; the rest read «واتَّبَعَتْهم» with the verb attributed to the offspring and with the feminine «تاء» added. The disagreement about the singular and plural of «ذُرِّيَّتهم» was treated thoroughly, praise be to Allah, in Sūrat al-Aʿrāf.
His saying: {أَلَتْنَاهُمْ}: Ibn Kathīr read «أَلِتْناهم» with kasra on the «لام», and the rest with fatḥa. The first is from «أَلِتَ يَأْلَتُ», with kasra on the middle radical in the past and fatḥa in the imperfect, like «عَلِمَ يَعْلَمُ».
As for the second, it may be from «أَلَتَ يَأْلِتُ» like «ضَربَ يَضْرِبُ», and it may be from «أَلات يُليت» like «أَماتَ يُميت», so «أَلَتْناهم» is like «أَمَتْناهم».
Ibn Hurmuz read «آلَتْناهم» with an «ألف» after the hamza, on the pattern «أَفْعَلْناهم». One says «آلَتَ يُؤْلِتُ» like «آمَنَ يُؤْمِنُ». ʿAbd Allāh, Ubayy, al-Aʿmash and Ṭalḥa, and it is also reported from Ibn Kathīr, read «لِتْناهم» with kasra on the «لام» like «بِعْناهم». One says «لاتَه يَليته» like «باعه يَبيعه».
Ṭalḥa and al-Aʿmash also read «لَتْناهم» with fatḥa on the «لام». Sahl said: "Fatḥa on the «لام» without an «ألف» is not permissible in any case", and for that reason he denied «آلَتْناهم» with the lengthening, and said: "Neither language nor exegesis indicates it." It is not as he claimed; rather the lexicographers reported «آلَتَ يُؤْلِتُ». It was also read «وَلَتْناهم» with «واو», like «وَعَدْناهم»; Hārūn reported it. Ibn Khālawayh said: "So this word is from «لاتَ يَليت», «وَلَتَ يَلِتَ», «أَلِتَ يَأْلَت», «أَلَت», and «أَلات يُليت». All of them mean to diminish. It is also said «أَلَتَ» in the sense of being harsh. A man stood up to admonish ʿUmar, and another man said to him: «لا تَأْلِتْ أميرَ المؤمنين», that is, do not be harsh with him." I say: it is possible that this report stands as it is, and the meaning is: do not diminish the Commander of the Believers' due, because if he is harsh with him in speech he diminishes his due.
His saying: {مِّنْ عَمَلِهِم مِّن شَيْءٍ}: «مِنْ شيءٍ» is the second object of «أَلَتْناهم», and «مِنْ» is redundant (zāʾida) in it. The first («من عملهم») is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl from «شيء», because originally it is an adjective of it; when it was put first it became accusative as a ḥāl. Abū al-Baqāʾ allowed it to be attached to «أَلَتْناهم», which is not apparent. As for the pronoun in «أَلَتْناهم», there are two views: the more apparent, that it refers to the believers; the second, that it refers to their sons. It was said that this is strengthened by His saying {كُلُّ امرىء بِمَا كَسَبَ رَهَينٌ}.

semin-durr:23-23.t: His saying: {يَتَنَازَعُونَ}: in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the object of «أَمَدَدْناهم»; it is also permissible that it be resumptive. The disagreement about His saying {لاَّ لَغْوٌ فِيهَا} was mentioned in al-Baqara. The clause is in the position of accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of «كأس», and His saying «فيها» means "in drinking it".

semin-durr:24-24.t: The clause {كَأَنَّهُمْ لُؤْلُؤٌ مَّكْنُونٌ} is a second naʿt (adjective) of «غِلمان».

semin-durr:25-25.t:
His saying: {يَتَسَآءَلُونَ}: a ḥāl (circumstantial) clause from «بعضُهم». The meaning of «يتنازَعون» is that they hand it to one another with a pulling to and fro, because that is the perfection of pleasure. He said:
4117 - نازَعْتُه طَيِّبَ الراحِ الشَّمولِ وقد ... صاح الدَّجاجُ وحانَتْ وَقْعَةُ السَّاري
(I passed back and forth with him the fine, chilled wine, when the cocks had crowed and the night-traveller's halt had come.)

semin-durr:27-27.t: His saying: {وَوَقَانَا}: the majority read it light; Abū Ḥaywa read it with shadda, as mentioned earlier. «السَّمُومُ» originally is the hot wind that penetrates the pores, plural «سَمائِم». One says «سُمَّ يومُنا», that is, its heat became intense. Thaʿlab said: "«السَّمومُ» is intense heat or intense cold in the daytime." Abū ʿUbayda said: "«السَّمومُ» is in the daytime, though it may be at night, and «الحَرور» is at night, though it may be in the daytime; «السموم» may also be used for the blast of cold, but it is more common for the blast of heat and sun." Something of this was mentioned earlier in Sūrat Fāṭir.

semin-durr:28-28.t: His saying: {إِنَّهُ هُوَ البر}: Nāfiʿ and al-Kisāʾī read it with fatḥa on the hamza, as a causal, that is, "because He". The rest read it with kasra, as resumptive containing the sense of cause, so the meaning of the two readings is the same.

semin-durr:29-29.t: His saying: {بِنِعْمَةِ رَبِّكَ}: There are three views on it. The first: that it is a thing sworn by, intervening between the ism of «ما» and its khabar, and the answer then is omitted, indicated by what is mentioned; the implied sense: "By the favour of your Lord, you are not a soothsayer nor a madman." The second: that the «باء» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), governed by «بكاهن» or «مجنون», the implied sense: "You are not a soothsayer or a madman, coupled with the favour of your Lord"; Abū al-Baqāʾ said this, and on this it is an inseparable ḥāl, because he, peace be upon him, never leaves this state. The third: that the «باء» is attached to what the speech indicates, and it is parenthetical between the ism of «ما» and its khabar; the implied sense: "You are not, in the state of your reminding, by the favour of your Lord, a soothsayer or a madman"; al-Ḥawfī said this. A fourth view appears: that the «باء» is causal, and is then attached to the content of the negated clause, and this is the intent of the noble verse. The meaning: soothsaying and madness are negated of you because of Allah's favour upon you, as you say «ما أنا بمُعْسِر بحمد الله وغَنائه» ("I am not in difficulty, thanks to Allah and His sufficiency").

semin-durr:30-30.t:
His saying: {أَمْ يَقُولُونَ}: Al-Thaʿlabī said: "Al-Khalīl said: every «أم» in Sūrat al-Ṭūr is an interrogative and not a conjunction." Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "«أم» in these verses is munqaṭiʿa (disjunctive)." I say: you were told earlier of the disagreement about the disjunctive: is it implied as «بل» alone, or «بل» and the hamza, or the hamza alone; the correct one is the second. Mujāhid said on His saying «أم تأمرهم»: its implied sense is «بل تأمرهم». And he read {بَلْ هُمْ قَوْمٌ طَاغُونُ} in place of «أم هم».
His saying: {نَّتَرَبَّصُ}: in the position of nominative as a naʿt (adjective) of «شاعر». The majority read «نتربَّصُ», with the verb attributed to a group of speakers, and «ريبَ» accusative. Zayd ibn ʿAlī read «يتربَّص» with yāʾ (two dots below) in the passive, and «ريبُ» nominative. «ريبُ المنونِ» are the events of time and the turns of fortune, because they do not endure in one state, like «الرَّيْب», which is doubt, for it does not remain but is shaky. The poet said:
4118 - تَرَبَّصْ بها رَيْبَ المنونِ لَعَلَّها ... تُطَلَّقُ يوماً أو يموتُ حليلُها
(Wait with her for the vicissitudes of fate; perhaps she will be divorced one day or her husband will die.)
And Abū Dhuʾayb said:
4119 - أمِن المَنونِ ورَيْبِه تتَوَجَّعُ ... والدهرُ ليس بمُعْتِبٍ مَنْ يَجْزَعُ
(Do you grieve over fate and its vicissitudes, while time grants no pardon to one who frets?)
«المنون» originally is time. Al-Rāghib said: "«المنون» is death, because it reduces the number and cuts the supply", and he counted among this His saying {أَجْرٌ غَيْرُ مَمْنُونٍ} [فصلت: 8], that is, not cut off. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It originally is a «فَعُول» from «مَنَّه» when he cut it, because death is cutting, and for this reason it is called «شَعُوب»." «ريبَ» is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), that is, "we await by him the events of time or death".

semin-durr:34-34.t: His saying: {بِحَدِيثٍ مِّثْلِهِ}: The majority read «حديث» with tanwīn and qualify it with «مثله». Al-Jaḥdarī and Abū al-Sammāl read «بحديثِ مثلِه», annexing «حديث» to «مثلِه», with an omitted qualified noun, that is, "with the speech of a man like him, of his kind".

semin-durr:35-35.t: His saying: {مِنْ غَيْرِ شَيْءٍ}: It is permissible that «مِنْ» denote the beginning of the range, in the sense: "or were they created from nothing living, like inanimate things, so that they are neither commanded nor forbidden, as inanimate things?" It was also said: it is causal, in the sense: "without cause, and not for the purpose of reward or punishment."

semin-durr:37-37.t:
His saying: {المصيطرون}: «المُسَيْطِرُ» is the overpowering, the dominant, from «سَيْطَرَ عليه» when one supervised, guarded or overpowered it. Only five words have come on the pattern «مُفَيْعِل»: four are attributes in the form of an active participle, like «مُهَيْمِن», «مُبَيْقِر», «مُسَيْطِر» and «مُبَيطِر», and one is the name of a mountain, which is «المُجَيْمِر». Imruʾ al-Qays said:
4120 - كأن ذُرا رأسِ المُجَيْمِرِ غُدْوَةً ... من السيلِ والغُثَّاءِ فَلْكَةُ مِغْزَلِ
(As if the heights of the summit of al-Mujaymir at morning, from the flood and its debris, were a spindle-whorl.)
The majority read «المُصَيْطِرون» with a pure «صاد», without a hint of «زاي» because of the «طاء», for the reason given earlier at {صِرَاطَ}. Hishām and Qunbul read it with the pure «سين», which is the original, without any disagreement from them; Ḥafṣ read so with disagreement from him. Khallād read it with a «صاد» hinting at «زاي» without disagreement from him. [Translator's note: the source then says that Khallād read both ways, "I mean like Khalaf and like the majority"; the repetition of the name Khallād here, and the reference to Khalaf, appear to be as in the source.] The justification of all these readings is clear from what was given you at the beginning of al-Fātiḥa.

semin-durr:38-38.t: His saying: {يَسْتَمِعُونَ}: a naʿt (adjective) of «سُلَّم». «وفيه» is in its usual locative sense. It was also said that it has the sense of «على», which is unnecessary. Al-Zamakhsharī implied it as attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), the implied sense being "ascending in it". The object of «يَسْتَمعون» is omitted; al-Zamakhsharī implied: "they listen to what is revealed to the angels of the knowledge of the unseen." Others implied: "they listen to the report confirming what they claim." The apparent view is that no object is implied for it, but the meaning is: "they bring about listening".

semin-durr:42-42.t: His saying: {فالذين كَفَرُواْ}: this is the placing of an overt noun in the place of a pronoun, to point to their being characterized by this ugly attribute. The original: "Or do they want a plot? Then they are the ones plotted against"; or it judges a genus of which they are a species, so that they fall under it first and foremost because of their deep involvement in this attribute.

semin-durr:44-44.t:
His saying: {وَإِن يَرَوْاْ}: this «إنْ» is conditional in its usual sense. It was also said that it has the sense of «لو», which is nothing.
His saying: {سَحَابٌ}: the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), that is, «هذا سحابٌ». The clause is accusative by the saying.

semin-durr:45-45.t:
His saying: {يُلاَقُواْ يَوْمَهُمْ}: «يَوْمَهم» is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), not an adverbial. Abū Ḥaywa read «يَلْقَوْا», the imperfect of «لَقِي». It is weak to say that the object is omitted and «يَوْمَهم» is an adverbial, that is, "they meet, or they encounter, the recompense of their deeds on their day."
His saying: {يُصْعَقُونَ}: Ibn ʿĀmir and ʿĀṣim read it with ḍamma on the yāʾ, in the passive; the rest of the Seven read it with fatḥa, in the active. Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān read it with ḍamma on the yāʾ and kasra on the «عين». As for the first, it may be from «صُعِقَ فهو مَصْعُوق», passive, which is triliteral, reported by al-Akhfash, so it is like «سُعِدوا»; and it may be from «أَصْعَقَ», quadriliteral. One says «أَصْعَق فهو مُصْعَق»; al-Fārisī said this. The meaning: others made them thunderstruck. The reading of al-Sulamī indicates that «أَفْعَلَ» has the sense of «فَعَل». His saying {يَوْمَ لاَ يُغْنِي} is a badal (substitute) from «يومَهم».

semin-durr:47-47.t: His saying: {وَإِنَّ لِلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُواْ}: It is permissible that it be a case of placing the overt noun in the place of the pronoun, and permissible that it not be, as discussed earlier.

semin-durr:48-48.t: His saying: {بِأَعْيُنِنَا}: the reading of the majority is with the two «نون»s separate. Abū al-Sammāl read it with the «نون» assimilated into what follows. The pluralizing of the pronoun here suits the plural «العين». Do you not see that He made it singular where He made «العين» singular in His saying {وَلِتُصْنَعَ على عيني} [طه: 39]? Al-Zamakhsharī said this.

semin-durr:49-49.t: His saying: {وَإِدْبَارَ النجوم}: The majority read it with kasra on the hamza as a maṣdar (verbal noun), unlike the one at the end of Sūrat Qāf, as mentioned earlier; for fatḥa is fitting there, since the plural of «دُبْر السجود», that is, its endings, is meant. However, Sālim al-Jaʿdī, Yaʿqūb and al-Minhāl ibn ʿAmr read it with fatḥa here, that is, "the ends of the stars". Their «إدبار» is when they set. And Allah knows best.
